name: system.power.cancel
description: Abort a pending in-process delayed shutdown / reboot / logoff scheduled via `delay_seconds`. Returns `ERR not_found` if no shutdown is pending.

cancelled_until_ms.description: Milliseconds remaining on the cancelled timer at the moment the cancel was applied. 0 if the timer was about to fire.

x-implementations.name: agent_native
x-implementations.description: Wakes the agent's pending-shutdown timer thread early so it skips the OS-level call. No OS API involvement; pure in-process state.

windows-modern.description: Cancels the agent's in-process delayed-shutdown timer. Capability-gated — agents without delayed-shutdown bookkeeping omit the verb from `system.capabilities`. The cancel is effective only on the agent that owns the timer; if a separate agent process scheduled the shutdown, this verb returns `ERR not_found`.

windows-classic.description: Same in-process timer-cancel mechanism as windows-modern. No NT-era API divergence — the timer is a managed in-agent thread regardless of OS version.
